skill.displayName: 弱电智能化投标决策-安防监控项目投标评估

llm.summary: The skill’s bid-analysis purpose is mostly coherent, but it adds persistent credential/account flows and exports shareable reports containing signed access links without enough containment.

dimensions.detail: Reading user-provided bid files and querying the vendor API are proportionate, but collecting platform/arch/MAC hash for account gating and creating shareable files with signed links is higher impact than necessary for bid analysis.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The manifest only declares ZLBX_API_KEY, while runtime instructions also read/write ~/.zlbx/config.json, write reports under ~/zlbx-bid-decision-files/, run a bundled Python renderer, and call vendor API/auth endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions disclose many behaviors and require consent before first auto-registration, but they also broadly route related procurement requests into the skill and require signed sk URLs to be carried into Markdown, JSON, and HTML outputs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists API keys in the user home directory, stores durable reports by default, and can generate auto-login recharge links tied to an API key source, creating credential and session-handling risk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core bid-decision workflow fits the stated purpose, but auto-registration, local API-key persistence, device-derived identifiers, recharge auto-login links, and mandatory preservation of signed access URLs materially expand the skill beyond analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with this skill contacting the vendor’s services, optionally creating an account after consent, storing an API key under your home directory, writing reports locally, and including signed vendor links in reports. Treat generated reports and their links as confidential.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Local reading of user-provided bid files and report generation are expected, but the metadata under-declares the additional config and report paths used at runtime.
[TP4] expected: The claimed analysis workflow is documented through API and workflow references; the report renderer is a support script, so the scanner’s implementation-mismatch concern is downgraded.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Auto-registration and credential lifecycle handling are disclosed and consent-gated initially, but they are account-management behavior rather than bid-analysis behavior.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Collecting a hashed MAC address and persisting an API key are disclosed, but they create stable device/account tracking and local secret-handling concerns.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Generating an auto-login recharge SID is outside the analytical workflow and introduces account/session transition risk.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The artifact explicitly requires preserving sk signed URLs in shareable outputs; this supports convenience but risks redistributing bearer-style access links.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The invocation description covers adjacent security/procurement requests even when the core domain term is absent, increasing unintended activation risk.
[SQP-2] expected: HTML export supports the reporting purpose, but making it the default creates persistent local business-intelligence artifacts without a separate opt-in step.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Preserving sensitive signed URL parameters in exported reports lacks adequate user warning for a report intended to be shared.
[SQP-2] expected: Reading a local bid document provided by the user is expected for bid analysis, but the instructions should more clearly restrict reads to user-selected files.
